fact: Uganda was elected to a four-year seat on the African Telecommunications Union Administrative Council at the ATU Conference of Plenipotentiaries in Abuja, dated 24 July 2026 by the Uganda Communications Commission.

The Ugandan delegation took part in the ATU Conference of Plenipotentiaries (CPL-26) in Abuja and spoke on the Union's 2027-2031 Strategic and Financial Plan and Risk Management Framework, per the Uganda Communications Commission.

Smart Africa, with Uganda's Ministry of ICT and National Guidance, held a national validation workshop in Kampala on Uganda's Digital Entrepreneurship and Innovation Country Assessment under AEDIB 2.0; the workshop date is not given, so the publication date is used.
The EACO statistics report names Uganda, through its regulator UCC, as one of seven member states submitting communications sector data to the East African Communications Organisation.

EACO reports Uganda's One Network Area inbound cross-border voice traffic fell 28.0% in 2025, from 1,103.2 million to 794.4 million minutes, which it attributes to over-the-top services substituting voice.

Uganda, which chairs the cluster, hosted in Kampala a Northern Corridor Integration Projects implementation clusters meeting with Kenya, Rwanda and South Sudan at which a joint account for a regional communications satellite feasibility study was reported open; the source gives no meeting date, so the report date 2026-08-24 is used.

A related-story teaser on the page, datelined Abuja 24 July 2026, and a headline dated 26 July 2026 state that Uganda won a seat on the African Telecommunications Union Administrative Council; the event date used is the teaser's dateline.
The ATU reports that the country is among 23 states that have endorsed the 49 African Common Proposals for the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference 2026.

fact: The EAC says the Regional E-Commerce Engagement Platform meeting of 13-15 October 2026 was chaired by Chris Matsiko of Uganda's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Cooperatives.
Smart Africa names Uganda among the 19 signatories of the SATA Declaration on digital trust and cross-border interoperability.
Uganda's parliamentary Committee on Foreign Affairs says Uganda has both signed and ratified the EAC Protocol on ICT Networks adopted in 2013.
Minister Rebecca Kadaga told Uganda's Parliament that the East African Payment System connects the national RTGS systems of Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania and Rwanda.

An EAC ICT and performance management professional told an EALA oversight meeting that Uganda is one of six of eight Partner States that have implemented the 2014 One Network Area roaming framework, which he said had helped reduce cross-border communication costs.
Uganda's ICT permanent secretary Aminah Zawedde chairs the Northern Corridor bloc's ICT and infrastructure cluster, which met in Kampala in August 2026.
The Northern Corridor ICT cluster reports the One Network Area, which scrapped roaming charges between member states, drove a more than 900-fold rise in roaming traffic.

Uganda's Ministry of ICT and National Guidance signed an MoU with the DRC Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy on 11 May 2026 on digital transformation, connectivity, cybersecurity and digital skills.
Uganda's Minister of ICT chaired the joint ministerial meeting of the Northern Corridor ICT Infrastructure Development cluster in Nairobi and coordinates the cluster.

The joint communique of the Northern Corridor Integration Projects ICT ministers (Kenya, Uganda, South Sudan, Rwanda) says One Network Area for voice, data and SMS is operational among the Partner States and has led to over 900 times traffic increase.
